concepts.title: Distance, Displacement and Position
concepts.definition: Motion is a change of position with time: the total path length travelled is distance, a scalar, while displacement is the straight-line change of position from start to end with its direction - they differ whenever the path bends or returns.
concepts.key_idea: Distance counts the road; displacement draws the arrow from start to finish.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc104.txt sections on distance and displacement
question_patterns: differentiate distance and displacement with an example
a body moves 4 m east and 3 m north - find distance and displacement

which of the two is a vector quantity and why
find the displacement of the object from the given description
draw the path and mark distance and displacement for the given motion

solution_steps.explain: Add the lengths of every stretch for distance.
Join start to end with an arrow for displacement.
Displacement never exceeds distance and carries direction.

concepts.title: Speed and Velocity
concepts.definition: Speed is the distance covered per unit time, while velocity is speed with direction - the rate of change of displacement; average speed uses total distance over total time, and uniform motion keeps both constant.
concepts.key_idea: Speed says how fast; velocity says how fast and which way.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc104.txt sections on speed and velocity
question_patterns: a car covers 150 km in 3 hours - find its speed
differentiate speed and velocity with an example
find the average speed from the given journey data
a runner completes one round of a circular track - what is the average velocity
calculate the velocity of the object from the given data
is the speed of the given motion uniform - justify

solution_steps.explain: Speed equals distance covered over the time taken.

concepts.title: Acceleration
concepts.definition: Acceleration measures how quickly velocity changes: it equals the change in velocity divided by the time taken, so speeding up, slowing down and turning are all accelerations, with units of metre per second squared.
concepts.key_idea: Change of velocity per second: negative acceleration means slowing down.
question_patterns: a bus speeds up from 5 m/s to 15 m/s in 4 s - find the acceleration
define acceleration with its unit
find the acceleration when velocity changes as given
can acceleration be negative - explain with an example
a body moves with uniform velocity - what is its acceleration
calculate the final velocity using acceleration and time

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the initial velocity u from the final velocity v.

concepts.title: Graphs of Motion
concepts.definition: Motion graphs make movement visible: a distance-time graph's slope gives speed - a rising straight line for uniform motion, a flat line for rest - while a velocity-time graph's slope gives acceleration and its area gives distance.
concepts.key_idea: Slope speaks: steep slope is fast motion, flat line is rest.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc104.txt sections on distance-time and velocity-time graphs
question_patterns: what does a straight line on a distance-time graph show
read the speed of the object from the given distance-time graph

identify rest, uniform and accelerated motion in the given graph
draw a distance-time graph for the given journey data

solution_steps.explain: Note which quantity sits on each axis.
Slope of distance-time gives speed; of velocity-time gives acceleration.
The area under a velocity-time graph gives distance covered.

worked_examples.question_pattern: An object covers {distance} m in {time} s. Find its speed.
A cyclist covers {distance} km in {time} hours. Calculate the speed in km/h.
The velocity of a scooter changes from {u} m/s to {v} m/s in {t} s. Find the acceleration.
A car starts from rest ({u} m/s) and reaches {v} m/s in {t} s. Calculate the acceleration.

solution_template.explain: Change per second is the acceleration.
